# Access security model

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask security-model` from conformance/catalog; do not edit. -->

This page states what Access guarantees, what it does not, who owns each remaining risk and how it is watched. Every row comes from the machine-readable catalogs in [`catalog/`](catalog), and `cargo xtask check` fails when this page and the catalogs differ.

## Verdict

**SECURE WITH DECLARED LIMITS.** The model holds semantically under attack; there is no model-level vulnerability. No compromised issuer, IdP, publisher, provider operator, executor or verifier can mint positive authority beyond its own declared blast radius: positive authority arises only from a meta-Exercise in an Anchor lineage (INV-1, INV-2), every external input passes a use-typed Acceptance (INV-15), and every actor attribution rests on an Actor Intent Statement signed with the actor Instance's KeyBinding (PI-7). The remaining risks are declared limits, not hidden ones, and the product never states them as guarantees (XI-12).

## Declared limits

Each limit is classed in the guarantee matrix and owned as a residual risk below.

| ID | Limit | Class |
|---|---|---|
| DL-1 | Custodian can impersonate Party unless custody is user-gated | Not guaranteed |
| DL-2 | Approval Surface operator can show misleading render for another digest | Not guaranteed |
| DL-3 | Use after revocation within declared offline window | Not guaranteed |
| DL-4 | Provider evaluation errors and equivocation only detectable, not preventable | Not guaranteed |
| DL-5 | Lost suffix in forced recovery | Not guaranteed |
| DL-6 | Authorized malicious or compromised actor can cause harm within authority | Not guaranteed |
| DL-7 | Decision surface acts as a policy oracle | Not guaranteed |
| DL-8 | Fail-closed halts consequential effects when Access is unavailable | Not guaranteed |
| DL-9 | Residual cross-domain and cross-RP linkability | Not guaranteed |
| DL-10 | Co-tenant side channels on shared compute infrastructure | Not guaranteed |

## Trust model

For each component: what it is trusted with, what it is never trusted with, the widest result if it is fully malicious, what it can never do (a boundary guaranteed by semantics) and the attributable lever that contains it.

| Component | Trusted with | Never trusted with | Blast radius | Never | Containment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Anchor root (sole or joint) | Being the source of authority within its own Anchor scope | Authority of another Anchor or domain | Everything in its own scope, within the rootTerms requirements | Act outside its scope; use a reserved action without the rootTerms requirement; erase history | Joint root (k-of-n) with delay; for a sole root, only a covering root or a new genesis |
| rootTerms domain.recover entry | Replacing the provider binding through forced recovery | Writing Grants, Acceptances or policy | Replacing the provider binding; a rollback attempt citing an old checkpoint fails the evaluator-side guard | Write authority state other than domain.recover; act from an anonymous request | Evaluator-side witness and replica checkpoint guard, witness and replica before ack, separate custody |
| Access provider (evaluator) | Producing decisions to the spec and keeping the records | Owning authority | Wrong ALLOW or DENY, denial of service, equivocation, lost suffix | Produce an Exercise on an actor's behalf without an AIS; own authority; rewrite history undetectably when a witness exists | domain.handover or domain.recover; detection by re-evaluation |
| Provider operator (including Suiss-hosted) | Running the provider | Being counted as root, custodian or surface owner | The provider's radius, plus DL-1 when it is also custodian and DL-2 when it also serves the surface | Hold authority not granted at genesis; impersonate Parties whose keys it does not hold | Separation of duties and user-gated custody |
| Provider signing key | Signing receipts, PAPs, checkpoints and metadata | Authority (custody attestation) | Forged current PAPs, receipts and tokens within each verifier's local acceptance ceiling until the recovery record reaches it | Make an online ADP decision; draw budget or record an Exercise centrally; be accepted after recovery without an exact-content inclusion proof | Verifier-side local ceilings and metadata freshness; domain.recover from the last verified checkpoint |
| Identity plane (issuer and custodian) | Issuing authentication, authenticator-binding and identity-binding Claims, as far as each is accepted | Creating authority | Impersonation up to the authority Parties already hold in the accepted subject class; designation changes when custodial | Create a Grant, an Acceptance, authority above a ceiling or a reserved action | Acceptance narrowing and ingest-time cutoff; a non-custodial controller |
| External IdP | The use it is accepted for | Any other use | Impersonation within the accepted subject class; selection within existing rule-shaped Grant ceilings | Create a Grant, an Acceptance or a meta-action | acceptance.amend cutoff |
| HR or claim issuer (subject selection) | Selection facts | Being a grantor | The holder set of rule-shaped Grants that already exist, within their ceilings | Exceed a Grant ceiling, reserved actions or budget | Cutoff as an affirmative disqualify |
| Schema publisher | The meaning of its namespace, as far as the exact accepted digest | Versions or mappings that were not accepted | The rendering and meaning of the accepted digest; mislabelling a pinned mapping | Change scope with a digest that was not accepted; drop a reserved flag silently | Revoke the schema-definition Acceptance (fails closed as schema-not-accepted) |
| Foreign domain | Evidence of authority within a foreign-authority Acceptance | Local authority | Up to the bridging Grant ceiling | Act outside the ceiling; write to the local record | Revoke the bridging Grant or Acceptance (exact locally) |
| PEP | Enforcing the decision before the effect (declared) | Being an actor | The effects it physically controls, which it could do without Access | Produce an actor signature to obtain ALLOW; carry a receipt to another intent | Revoke the verifier or PEP Acceptance; domain operations |
| Offline verifier | Following the contract (declared) | The accuracy of its reports | Contracts in its own audience, up to horizon and slice | Spend a slice a second time centrally; obtain a new contract after its profile Acceptance is revoked | Revoke the predicate-input Acceptance; issuer-side refusal |
| Executor | Asking at continuation and declaring stop | The truth of an effect (a Claim) | Continuing running work; false attestation | Request continuation on its own behalf; release on its own | Instance restriction or termination; revoke the attestation issuer Acceptance |
| Approval Surface | Faithful rendering and collecting the user's act (declared) | Detecting from the record that the rendering was faithful | Collecting assertions from its own users for a different intent (DL-2) | Contribute without the approver's AIS and assertion; approve past a DENY | Surface conformance Acceptance; the independent surface requirement |
| Relay or SSF transmitter | Delivery (best effort) | Any security decision | Delayed, lost or forged events | Widen authority | Receiver re-query; event signatures |
| Work or coordinator | Gates and attention management | Satisfying an Access requirement | Misrouting approval requests; bombarding approvers | Create authority; pass a DENY through a Gate | Work's own controls; the Access request rate policy |
| One, agent or model | Exercising within its own Instance and Mandate | Being a source of instructions | Everything within Grant, Mandate and budget | Grant, widen or approve without the user's Instance | Mandate revoke, instance.terminate, suspend |
| Witness | Co-signing checkpoints faithfully | Authority | False co-signatures; hiding equivocation when it is the only witness | Change authority state | Witness diversity (at least two); the domain replaces the witness |
| Protocol governance | Publishing the core spec and meta-schema | Taking effect in a domain on its own | Publishing a bad core version | Affect a domain that does not adopt it | The domain does not adopt it (adoption is a reserved root meta-Exercise) |
| Party controller | Managing the Party's key state and issuer designation | Authority (controller is not authority) | The Party's Instance setup and issuer designation | Write a Grant | Regime recovery of the Party |
| Realm JOSE or SAML signing key (identity plane) | Signing authentication results for its own realm's relying parties | Signing authority artefacts; any other realm | Golden SAML or forged ID tokens for any user at every relying party of the realm until rotation; on the Access side only as far as the authentication use | Create authority; write a Grant or Acceptance; be valid at another realm's relying party | Key rotation and removal from the JWKS (key_epoch increment), issuer cutoff, HSM or signer process |
| Operational signing key (domain-scoped, separate signer process) | Signing its own domain's PAP, receipt and checkpoint excerpts within its lifetime | Another domain; changing the binding | Forged PAPs and receipts in its own domain, within the key lifetime and each verifier's local ceiling | Be accepted in another domain; stand in for the binding key | key_epoch increment; domain.recover; rebuild the signer process |
| Binding key (HSM, quorum) | Signing the Domain Metadata binding and operational key delegation | Everyday signing | The provider signing key's radius plus operational key authorisation | Be used without quorum (HSM policy) | domain.recover; HSM quorum change |
| LDAP, Kerberos, RADIUS or WS-Fed gateway process | Turning a legacy protocol bind into an identity plane authentication event | Authority; credentials other than passwords | Passwords of users who bind through it (it sees cleartext); forged authentication for that realm | Leave its realm; reach the signer key (separate process and sandbox profile); let the Kerberos C FFI reach the main process memory | Close the gateway; reset credentials for affected users; realm cutoff |
| SCIM client (inbound provisioning) | The subject-selection and identity-binding attributes declared in its Acceptance | Being a grantor | As for an HR or claim issuer: selection within existing rule-shaped Grant ceilings; stale positive Claims | Exceed a Grant ceiling | Revoke the SCIM token; Acceptance cutoff |
| Parser worker (SAML/XML and, where needed, BER or CBOR; isolated process) | Turning input into a normalised structure | Deciding a signature verification result alone; key material | Accepting a forged assertion through XSW-class misparsing in the realm it serves; crashing (denial of service) | Reach the signer or the main process memory (separate process, no network syscalls) | Restart the worker; XSW regression corpus; roll back the parser version |
| Co-tenant (another tenant or workload on the same physical host) | Nothing | Everything | Secret leakage through microarchitectural side channels (DL-10) | Change authority, a record or a decision (a side channel only affects confidentiality) | Dedicated compute; mitigations=auto,nosmt |
| Support staff (support access) | Reading and acting within the support Grant the user gave | Producing an AIS on the user's behalf (no impersonation) | The scope and duration of the support Grant | Sign in as the user; act outside the Grant | Revoke the support Grant; expiry |

## Known hard limits

No hard limit is ever part of a product promise. Each one names the honest wording that replaces a claim the product must not make.

| ID | Hard limit | Honest wording |
|---|---|---|
| HL-1 | Per-domain throughput limited by single sequencer | Same hardware budget and Argon2 cost, target: X (pending reproduction). |
| HL-2 | Wrong decisions by provider or operator cannot be prevented | Equivocation is detectable with independent witnesses, not preventable. Silent corruption is detected against commitments; decisions before detection are not covered. |
| HL-3 | Revocation delayed during offline window | Offline verifiers honor revocation within their declared freshness window. |
| HL-4 | Lost suffix in forced recovery, including slice double-spend | Changes after <time of N> may be lost; repeat revocations made after then. |
| HL-5 | Client cannot know outcome on timeout |  |
| HL-6 | Drift if all time sources and witnesses lie together | Time terms rely on independent time sources and witnesses. |
| HL-7 | Equivocation detectable but not preventable |  |
| HL-8 | Correlated breach via shared HSM partition or cross-domain key acceptance |  |
| HL-9 | No physical erasure; redaction is not erase |  |
| HL-10 | Merkle index reveals position | An inclusion proof reveals the record's position (its leaf index) in the log and the log size. |
| HL-11 | Status list herd privacy bounded by list size | A status list hides a token only among the other entries of the same list; the herd is never larger than the list. |
| HL-12 | Cross-implementation determinism limited to test vector coverage | Implementations agree on the published test vectors and the differential runs; beyond their coverage agreement is not guaranteed. |
| HL-13 | Revocation does not stop an already running effect | Authority revoked. Agent: running / paused (confirmed) / unknown. |
| HL-14 | TEE/SE side channels and hardware lying about secure clock | Offline reports are the reporting verifier's claim. |
| HL-15 | Async runtime and HTTP layer outside formal verification | The async runtime and the HTTP layer are outside the formal models; fuzzing, deterministic simulation and tests cover them. |
| HL-16 | Compiler and CPU do not guarantee constant-time execution | Constant-time code is measured (dudect, ctgrind, assembly snapshots); neither the compiler nor the CPU guarantees it. |
| HL-17 | Co-tenant side channels on shared hardware, Postgres or cache | On shared hardware co-tenant side channels remain possible; dedicated compute is the option that removes them. |
| HL-18 | Residual cross-domain linkability via KeyBinding, timing, network | Each app sees a different user number; timing, network and device data may still allow correlation. |
| HL-19 | No PQC in WebAuthn/passkeys; new assertions forgeable post-CRQC | Passkeys don't use post-quantum cryptography yet; after a cryptographically relevant quantum computer new assertions could be forged. |
| HL-20 | HSM/KMS throughput ceiling and correlated shared quota exhaustion | Signing throughput is bounded by the declared HSM/KMS ceiling. |
| HL-21 | In-memory secrets readable on host compromise beyond zeroize | A host compromise exposes keys in process memory for the declared window. Secrets are zeroized on drop; copies in registers, swap or dumps are not covered. |
| HL-22 | Stateless token revocation not effective before expiry at RS |  |
| HL-23 | Phishing-resistant authentication does not prevent session or token theft | Passkeys are origin-bound and phishing-resistant; device binding separately protects against session theft. A passkey sign-in can't be relayed through a phishing proxy; it does not stop theft of the session or token after sign-in, and password with TOTP can be relayed. |
| HL-24 | No registry publisher signatures; supply chain attacks only detectable and containable | Registry publisher identity is trust-on-first-use; dependencies are reviewed and vendored. |
| HL-27 | FIPS and PQ profiles cannot be combined (no FIPS ML-DSA) | FIPS and post-quantum profiles can't be combined; a realm or domain picks one of them. |
| HL-29 | Formal assurance limited to proof scope | Property P of model M is machine-checked (Lean, Kani or TLA+); see the formal scope for what is outside it. |
| HL-31 | Identity plane async DR has RPO greater than zero |  |
| HL-32 | Identity plane restores whole clusters, never one tenant or realm alone |  |
| HL-33 | Postgres superuser and RLS-exempt roles escape DB-level protections |  |
| HL-34 | Binding re-anchor must precede old binding key compromise | A binding re-anchor protects history only when it happens before the old binding key is compromised. |
| HL-35 | Leaked realm signing key enables Golden SAML-style forgery | Whoever holds a leaked realm signing key can forge ID tokens and SAML assertions for that realm until the key is rotated out of the JWKS and the metadata. |
| HL-36 | Client identity takeover via expired or resold CIMD domain | A CIMD client is whoever controls its domain; an expired or resold domain hands the client identity to the new owner until the realm policy drops that domain. |
| HL-37 | MCP server tenant isolation logic bugs cause cross-tenant disclosure | Guarantees hold for conformant PEPs (SDK or declared conformance). |
| HL-38 | Help desk social engineering and contact channel loss |  |
| HL-39 | Product invitation email abused as phishing channel |  |
| HL-40 | Single-node profile may lose acked writes on node/disk loss |  |
| HL-41 | New tenants can configure CT2+ without SEC18 cooling |  |

| ID | Risk | Owner | Why accepted | Signal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RR-1 | Custodian impersonation in custodial mode | Identity plane (custodian) and the domain | Usability; the non-custodial option is always open | `none-declared` |
| RR-2 | Unfaithful or compromised approval surface | Surface operator; the domain (Acceptance) | An authenticator cannot show content | `audit:spc.mismatch` |
| RR-3 | Abuse within offline or intermittent window | The domain (contract issuer) and the verifier operator | Connectivity is a fact of the deployment | `none-declared` |
| RR-4 | Provider wrong decision or equivocation | Provider; the domain (witness, re-evaluation) | The provider's decision is physically in its hands | `event:witness.equivocation.detected`, `alert:AccessWitnessEquivocation`, `event:replay.divergence.found` |
| RR-5 | Lost suffix without witness or replica | Domain root | Witness and off-provider replica are optional (mandatory in the Suiss-hosted template) | `event:replica.lag`, `event:checkpoint.witness.pending`, `audit:replica.lagging` |
| RR-6 | Authorized malicious actor or collusion | Domain governance; Work accountability | Approved is not the same as wise | `metric:access_requester_throttled_total` |
| RR-7 | Policy oracle threshold inference | The domain (policy design); security tooling | Determinism forbids random noise in decisions | `metric:access_advisory_requests_total` |
| RR-8 | Availability cost of fail-closed | The domain (continuity plan); the provider | Security comes before availability | `metric:access_protocol_rejections_total`, `metric:access_decisions_total` |
| RR-9 | Ambiguous publisher mapping semantics | Publisher; domain admins | Access cannot verify meaning | `audit:authority.decision.require_action` |
| RR-10 | Sole root compromise | Root Party | Simplicity of personal domains | `none-declared` |
| RR-11 | Denial of service through narrowing | The domain (restriction scope) | The deliberate cost of narrowing always being allowed | `audit:incident.contained` |
| RR-12 | Prompt injection or model error within Grant and Mandate | Agent operator; One and Executor | Models make mistakes; Access bounds, it does not prevent | `none-declared` |
| RR-13 | Effects executed during compromise window | Effect owners (Pay, the domain, Executor) | Recovery is prospective | `none-declared` |
| RR-14 | Forged PAP/receipt acceptance before provider key theft detected | Provider operator (key custody); the domain (local ceilings, recovery); verifier operators | The key is not the evaluator; containment is only possible at the verifier | `event:witness.equivocation.detected`, `alert:AccessWitnessEquivocation` |
| RR-15 | Party unaware of un-ingested regime key events | Party Identity Regime (Work and Access governance) | Key-event history belongs to the regime | `none-declared` |
| RR-16 | No formally verified Argon2 implementation | Identity plane (credential store); security team | Industry-standard password hash with no alternative; passkeys are the primary factor | `ci:nightly/audit` |
| RR-17 | No verified RS256 implementation; Marvin flaw unpatched in rsa crate | Identity plane | Opt-in per client only, through aws-lc-rs; authority artefacts are never RSA | `ci:nightly/audit` |
| RR-18 | OAuth/OIDC AS written from scratch in Rust | Identity plane engineering | Single-backend decision; compensated by differential tests and the OIDF suite | `ci:conformance/oidf-conformance`, `ci:conformance/differential` |
| RR-19 | Correlated single-maintainer critical dependencies (bus factor) | Supply chain owner | Rust ecosystem reality; vendoring and fork readiness | `ci:ci/supply-chain`, `ci:nightly/supply-chain-watch` |
| RR-20 | SAML/XML complexity: c14n, signature wrapping, libxml2-class bugs | Identity plane (SAML gateway) | SAML is in scope; isolated parser worker; DocType refused | `ci:nightly/test-full`, `ci:conformance/interop-lab` |
| RR-21 | Malicious packages via unsigned crates.io/npm publishing | Supply chain owner | Registry reality; detection and containment | `ci:ci/supply-chain`, `ci:nightly/audit`, `ci:nightly/npm-audit` |
| RR-22 | Residual linkability via claims, cnf keys and timing | Identity plane; the domain (attribute disclosure policy) | Network and timing information cannot be erased by cryptography | `metric:access_public_sub_opt_in_total` |
| RR-23 | Co-tenant side channel | Hosting operator; the tenant (dedicated choice) | Cost; the dedicated option is open | `none-declared` |
| RR-24 | Account enumeration timing channel | Identity plane | Measurement threshold under network jitter | `ci:nightly/test-full` |
| RR-25 | Pre-signed tokens accepted until expiry during identity degraded window | Identity plane; RS operator | Availability; the window is the declared token lifetime | `metric:access_identity_degraded_seconds`, `alert:AccessIdentityDegradedLong` |
| RR-26 | Compiler breaks constant-time code | Security team | The compiler gives no constant-time guarantee | `ci:nightly/dudect`, `ci:nightly/ctgrind` |
| RR-27 | Bugs in async/HTTP layer outside formal scope | Engineering | Tool maturity | `ci:nightly/test-full` |
| RR-28 | Kerberos C FFI introduces memory-unsafe code | Gateway owner | Kerberos compatibility; isolated process | `ci:weekly/kerberos-asan` |
| RR-29 | Phishable authentication factors (TOTP, push, SMS) | The domain (factor policy); identity plane | Regulation and user reality; CT2+ needs a phishing-resistant factor | `metric:access_sign_in_factor_total` |
| RR-30 | Post-authentication token or session theft, including DPoP key misuse | Identity plane; RS | A passkey protects the sign-in, not the session after it; DPoP and DBSC narrow it | `audit:session.device_mismatch` |
| RR-31 | HSM/KMS throughput and quota correlation | Provider operator | Hardware and cloud reality | `metric:access_signer_call_duration_seconds`, `alert:AccessSignerSlow` |
| RR-32 | Missing post-quantum support in WebAuthn | Standards bodies; identity plane (watching) | No standard exists | `none-declared` |
| RR-33 | Unclear CRA classification and manufacturer scope | Suiss management | Decision pending; preparation follows the Class I default | `none-declared` |
| RR-34 | Fake or inflated security data used as decision input | Security team | Every number is source-labelled and unverified ones are marked | `none-declared` |
| RR-35 | Records before PQ re-anchor lack PQ-verifiable existed-by-T | The domain (PQ profile and cadence); the provider (re-anchor production) | The CRQC date is unknown; re-anchoring is periodic | `none-declared` |
| RR-36 | Harvest-now-decrypt-later on encrypted identity tokens | The realm (JWE use) and the RP | There is no PQ KEM standard for JOSE | `none-declared` |
| RR-37 | Immature ML-DSA implementations may accept forged signatures | The provider (library choice); the domain (PQ profile) | Maturity takes time | `ci:nightly/f0-differential` |
| RR-38 | Managed platforms may lack memory hardening backends | Provider or self-host operator | Platform limits | `metric:access_secret_memory_backend` |
| RR-39 | Unused; reserved ID | None (reserved ID) | Reserved; never reused | `none-declared` |
| RR-43 | Brokered upstream tokens stay bearer due to missing DPoP support | Identity plane (broker); the domain (upstream connection choice) | Upstream ecosystem reality; the CT2+ default is broker-as-PEP | `none-declared` |
| RR-44 | Mainstream MCP clients limited to Public scope until AIS support | Product; MCP PEP owner | PI-11 is frozen; bearer authority is never given | `none-declared` |
| RR-45 | RP ID change invalidates passkeys, forcing weakest recovery path | The tenant (domain name decision); identity plane | WebAuthn binds passkeys to the RP ID | `metric:access_recovery_weakest_path_total` |

A signal is an alert (`alert:`), a logged event (`event:`, `audit:`), a metric (`metric:`) or a CI job (`ci:<workflow>/<job>`); `none-declared` means no signal is declared yet.

## Formal scope

Each line is a property of a model, machine-checked by the named tool; nothing outside the model is covered (HL-29). The async runtime, the HTTP layer, the compiler and the CPU are outside it (HL-15, HL-16).

|---|---|---|---|
| ⊑ on bounds is reflexive | `Access.boundLe_refl` | L0-ALG-5 | machine-checked (Lean) |
| ⊑ on bounds is transitive | `Access.boundLe_trans` | L0-ALG-5 | machine-checked (Lean) |
| ⊑ on bounds is sound: a value within the child bound is within the parent bound | `Access.withinB_mono` | L0-ALG-5 | machine-checked (Lean) |
| a ∩ b ⊑ a and a ∩ b ⊑ b for bounds | `Access.boundMeet_le` | L0-ALG-5 | machine-checked (Lean) |
| every well-formed lower bound of two bounds is below their ∩ | `Access.boundMeet_greatest` | L0-ALG-5 | machine-checked (Lean) |
| normalize on bounds is idempotent | `Access.boundNorm_idem` | L0-ALG-5 | machine-checked (Lean) |
| a normalized bound allows exactly the values the bound allows | `Access.boundNorm_within` | L0-ALG-5 | machine-checked (Lean) |
| ⊑ on authority sets is reflexive on well-formed values (unique parameter keys) | `Access.authLe_refl` | L0-ALG-5, OP-124 m.2 | machine-checked (Lean) |
| ⊑ on authority sets is transitive | `Access.authLe_trans` | L0-ALG-5 | machine-checked (Lean) |
| if c ⊑ p, every intent c covers is covered by p | `Access.authLe_sound` | L0-ALG-5 | machine-checked (Lean) |

| every lower bound that covers some action and has well-formed bounds is below a ∩ b | `Access.authMeet_greatest_wf` | L0-ALG-5, L0-ALG-51 | machine-checked (Lean) |

## Conformance and certification

The conformance suite runs without a Suiss account and without network access to Suiss: the vectors, the reference evaluator and the PEP runner are in this folder, and the PEP runner only talks to fake upstreams on the loopback interface. Suiss-hosted Access is held to the same suite, which CI runs against our own server. Passing a profile is a published test result for named vectors; conformance is not endorsement. Suiss sells no certification or assessment service, and an audit of Access is never sold as a Suiss certificate.
